cards.heading: DNS
cards.body: DNS turns names into addresses. A client asks its configured DNS server, which answers from its cache or resolves the name through the root, TLD and authoritative servers. Queries normally use UDP 53 (TCP 53 for large answers and zone transfers).
cards.example:
A     www.example.com → 93.184.216.34
AAAA  IPv6 address
CNAME alias → another name
MX    mail server for a domain
PTR   address → name (reverse lookup)

cards.heading: DNS on a router
cards.body: A router can resolve names for its own commands (ping a name) with a name server, or you can disable lookups so a mistyped command isn't treated as a hostname.
cards.example:
ip name-server 8.8.8.8
ip domain-lookup
! or: no ip domain-lookup

cards.heading: DHCP: DORA
cards.body: A client gets its IP settings in four messages: Discover (client broadcast), Offer (server), Request (client), Ack (server). The client uses UDP 68, the server UDP 67. Leases expire and are renewed.

cards.heading: A router as DHCP server
cards.body: Exclude addresses you assign statically (gateways, servers, printers) globally, then define a pool for the subnet with its gateway and DNS server.
cards.example:
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.10
ip dhcp pool LAN10
 network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.10.1
 dns-server 8.8.8.8

cards.heading: DHCP relay
cards.body: A Discover is a broadcast, and routers don't forward broadcasts, so clients on a subnet without a DHCP server need a relay. 'ip helper-address' on the router interface facing the clients forwards their requests as unicast to the server, filling in giaddr (the interface's address) so the server picks the right pool.
cards.example:
interface g0/1
 ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
 ip helper-address 10.0.12.1

cards.heading: Router as DHCP client and verification
cards.body: A router interface can get its own address by DHCP, typically from an ISP. On the server, 'show ip dhcp binding' lists leases and 'show ip dhcp pool' the pools.
